page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8i.large is a compute-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It is provisioned with 2 dedicated vCPUs running on an Intel Xeon 8475B processor based on the x86_64 architecture with a base clock frequency of 2.7 GHz. System memory totals 4.0 GB, yielding a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU, aligning with compute-focused workload profiles.

The instance configuration includes 2 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth and does not feature complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Dedicated local storage is absent, meaning storage requirements rely entirely on attached remote block volumes. Additionally, the instance operates without discrete GPU hardware acceleration, constraining its profile to CPU-centric tasks.

Due to the 1:2 ratio of compute cores to memory capacity, the server provides cost-effective dedicated compute capability without incurring unnecessary memory overhead. Primary operational tradeoffs include reliance on external network volumes for persistent data and restricted memory boundaries. The instance is suited for batch processing tasks, web serving, microservices, light continuous integration jobs, and distributed worker nodes that do not demand large in-memory working sets.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8i.large is an entry-tier compute-optimized instance hosted on KVM virtualization. Powered by a 2.7 GHz Intel Xeon 8475B processor on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 2 dedicated vCPUs paired with 4.0 GB of memory, maintaining a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not feature local storage or discrete graphics hardware, requiring external cloud block storage for file systems and data persistence. Connectivity includes 2 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses included. By avoiding excessive memory capacity, the configuration offers an efficient compute allocation for processing workloads. It is appropriate for lightweight compute-intensive services, web tier nodes, API backends, build runners, and batch execution pipelines where substantial RAM or local IOPS are not required.
